tagline: Qatar's capital has raced from pearl-diving port to World Cup host, stacking I.M. Pei's Museum of Islamic Art, the lanes of Souq Waqif and the futuristic Corniche skyline along the Gulf.
overview: Doha was a small pearling and fishing port until oil and then vast natural gas wealth made Qatar one of the richest countries on Earth per person. The city has grown at extraordinary speed, capped by hosting the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the first in the Middle East.

The Corniche promenade curves along the bay between the traditional dhow harbour and the towers of West Bay. At its heart sits the Museum of Islamic Art, I.M. Pei's geometric masterwork, while the National Museum of Qatar, shaped like a desert rose crystal, tells the country's story. Souq Waqif's restored lanes sell spices, textiles and falcons, and stay lively late into the night.

Beyond the city, Qatar's signature adventure is the desert: dune-bashing tours race down sand walls to the Inland Sea, Khor Al Adaid, where the sea floods in among the dunes. Back in town, The Pearl island, Katara Cultural Village and the new Lusail district show where the city is heading next.

funFacts.title: A WORLD CUP FIRST
funFacts.text: Doha hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup, the first World Cup held in the Middle East.

funFacts.title: I.M. PEI'S MASTERPIECE
funFacts.text: The Museum of Islamic Art was designed by I.M. Pei, the architect of the Louvre pyramid, at age 91.

funFacts.title: WHERE THE SEA MEETS THE DUNES
funFacts.text: Khor Al Adaid, the Inland Sea, is a UNESCO-recognised reserve reachable only through the desert.

funFacts.title: A DESERT ROSE
funFacts.text: The National Museum of Qatar's interlocking discs were inspired by the desert rose crystal.

funFacts.title: FALCONS HAVE A SOUQ
funFacts.text: Souq Waqif has a dedicated falcon market and even a hospital for the prized birds.

funFacts.title: A CITY OF NEWCOMERS
funFacts.text: Around 9 in 10 of Qatar's residents are expatriates from around the world.

funFacts.title: SEVEN KILOMETRES OF CORNICHE
funFacts.text: The Doha Corniche waterfront promenade runs about 7 kilometres around the bay.

funFacts.title: AN ARTIFICIAL RIVIERA
funFacts.text: The Pearl-Qatar is a man-made island of marinas, towers and Mediterranean-style streets.

funFacts.title: HOME OF AL JAZEERA
funFacts.text: The Al Jazeera news network, launched in 1996, is headquartered in Doha.

funFacts.title: A NEW CITY NAMED LUSAIL
funFacts.text: Lusail City, built for the World Cup final stadium, was planned from scratch north of Doha.
